Remember when a computer felt simple? Verse OS carries that spirit forward: a clear desktop, direct interactions, and software that leaves room for your ideas.

Built on Haiku and developed on the Milk-V Pioneer, Verse explores what a personal operating system can be on RISC-V—with local AI as part of the experience, not a distant service.

Explore the source ↗

Built in the open

A real desktop.
An ongoing experiment.

01

RISC-V, on real hardware

The Pioneer port has reached a working desktop with 64 CPUs, keyboard, mouse, networking, and SSD boot support.

02

AI that stays with you

A native chat app connects to a resident llama.cpp service and a local Qwen model. Desktop actions ask for your permission.

03

Space to keep improving

Performance, reliability, and packaging are active work. Tenstorrent accelerator support is being investigated—not yet supported.

For the curious

Start with the source.

Verse OS is an experimental distribution in development, not a finished general-purpose release. A ready-to-install public image is not offered here yet.

Want to build or follow along? The Pioneer repository contains the source, build tools, and development notes. Use separate test storage and keep a recovery system available.
